scope: Trusted private session configuration, command lifecycle, async request binding, database path hygiene and neutral metadata projection.

findings.independentReproduction: The original source validated and audited a first planned episode, then dispatched a different planned episode after the caller changed request.episodeId during asynchronous local factory creation.
findings.fix: Author snapshots the scalar request fields at command entry before the first await.
findings.verification: The same async barrier/mutation control now dispatches the originally requested episode and its command audit agrees.

findings.independentReproduction: With an invented plan placed at dispatcherDatabase plus -wal, the original command accepted the configuration, ran its synthetic metadata callback, and SQLite later deleted the temporary plan input.
findings.fix: Author rejects config, plan and readiness input paths that equal either database main path or either database's WAL, SHM or rollback-journal sidecar before constructing a database.
findings.verification: Six plan-sidecar combinations and eight config main/sidecar combinations reject; all original input bytes remain intact and no runtime factory is constructed.

additionalControls: Status and terminal-row replay invoke neither the factory nor the current-source hook.
Cancellation during local factory preparation prevents entry into the synthetic execution callback and closes local resources.
A returned transport identity mismatch closes resources once and creates no terminal result or synthetic execution.
A stale uninitialized session marker cannot adopt dispatcher state containing an executed episode.
Missing initialized dispatcher state and an orphan dispatcher each reject before another factory is created.
Factory public projections contain neither the invented oracle identity nor private plan/config paths; augmented or changed inputs cannot obtain a reservation projection.
Cancel and recover commands use control callbacks and preserve all 72 planned identities.
A close failure after synthetic execution produces a sanitized unknown execution flag and a terminal episode cannot be replayed.
limits: All plans, callbacks, state and path collisions were invented within temporary private directories; no real data was deleted.
Synthetic metadata callbacks returned no candidate. No provider, repair, candidate execution or sealed-corpus content was used.
The independent session controls do not execute the live transport branch or authenticate a provider, readiness declaration, USD amount or cleanup observation.
Creation and close of an injected factory must remain local and nonbillable as required by the documented contract; this module cannot enforce arbitrary trusted callback behavior.
Same-UID tampering and coordinated rollback of both durable databases remain outside consistency guarantees.
The author's broader session tests and later root integration checks are separate from the independent commands recorded here.
